summary: Phase 0 backend testing of Grizedale rota solver. Tested all 3 endpoints (/api/health, /api/solver/seed, /api/solver/generate) plus /api/docs and /api/openapi.json. Validated hard rules (cover counts, med/FA per shift, no-male-pair, capability flags, consecutive-day rules), forced cells (locked + AL), input validation (400), over-constrained handling (422), and the manager weekday soft-penalty. 14/14 pytest tests pass.

minor.issue: Seed limitation (NOT a code bug): C.E. is the ONLY medication-competent staff who can also do nights/sleepover (J.C./L.M./L.D./T.D. all have can_do_nights=false, A.A. and J.R. are not med_competent). Putting C.E. on AL on any single day makes night-shift med coverage infeasible -> solver correctly returns 422 with reason 'no medication-competent staff available for night shift'. Main-agent's spec test expected 200 for {C.E., 2026-04-22, AL}; that scenario is mathematically infeasible with this seed. I added a replacement test using D.A. on AL to verify the AL mechanism itself, and a separate test asserting the C.E. case correctly returns 422.

FastAPI HTTPException would wrap the body under {detail: ...}, but the implementation uses JSONResponse(status_code=422, content=result), so the failure body is returned at the top level (success/reason/blocking_constraints). Tests handle both shapes; no fix needed.

action_items: Decide on the C.E.-AL test case: either (a) accept that med-competent night coverage is a hard bottleneck of the current seed and update the spec to use D.A./A.A. for AL examples, or (b) add med_competent=true to A.A. or another night-capable staff so the rota can absorb a single C.E. AL day without going infeasible. This will also affect Phase 1+ realism — only one med-competent staff covering 28 nights leaves zero buffer for sickness/holiday.

Optional polish: solver/generate currently returns 400 via HTTPException (body = {detail: '...'}) but 422 via JSONResponse (body at top-level). Consider unifying so clients see a consistent envelope (e.g. always {success, reason, ...}).
Manager soft-penalty (W_MANAGER_WEEKDAY=10000) is dominating other terms — verified J.C. is OFF on every Mon-Fri in the optimal solution, as required.
critical_code_review_comments: rota_solver.py is ~450 lines and self-contained — fine for Phase 0 but should be split into model_builder / objective / response modules before adding Phase 1 features.
Hours soft penalty (W_HOURS_DEVIATION=5) is symmetric (over and under same weight). For UK care-home compliance it might matter more to under-staff than over — flag for product owner.
POST /api/solver/generate accepts dict[str, Any] with no Pydantic schema. Phase 0 acceptable, but for Phase 1 a typed RotaRequest model would surface bad input earlier and improve /api/docs.

MongoDB client is initialised at import time even though Phase 0 doesn't use it; a missing MONGO_URL would crash the whole app on boot. Acceptable since env is set, but worth wrapping when Phase 1 adds optional persistence.

_build_failure_response() iterates each day for blocking analysis but doesn't account for cross-day constraints (consecutive-day, weekly hours) — its own docstring says so. Good enough for Phase 0 but list it as known limitation in PRD.
Solver uses num_search_workers=8 with max_time_in_seconds=10. With seed it solves in <30 ms so no concern; once seed grows, ensure deterministic seed for reproducible tests.
seed_data_creation: Used /app/backend/seed/grizedale.json as-is. Test cases mutate copies in-memory; seed file untouched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 14 pytest tests in /app/backend/tests/test_rota_solver.py pass against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Solver wall-time is consistently <100 ms with the seed (well under 15s SLA). Endpoints covered: GET /api/health, GET /api/solver/seed, GET /api/docs, GET /api/openapi.json, POST /api/solver/generate (success path, capability flags, consecutive-day rules, locked cells, AL mechanism, over-constrained 422, missing-field 400, manager weekday soft penalty). The C.E.-AL spec scenario was replaced with an equivalent test using D.A. because the seed has only one med-competent night-capable staff (C.E.); see backend_issues.minor for details.
rca_of_the_issue: Spec test 'C.E. AL on 2026-04-22 returns 200' fails because the seed contains only one staff member (C.E.) who satisfies BOTH medication_competent=true AND (can_do_nights or can_do_sleepover)=true. Hard rule 'every night must have >=1 med-competent staff' therefore depends entirely on C.E. for night cover. Removing her for any single day makes the model INFEASIBLE — solver correctly responds 422 with blocking_constraint 'no medication-competent staff available for night shift'. Mitigation: either change the spec to use a non-bottleneck staff (e.g. D.A.) or expand the seed (e.g. set A.A.medication_competent=true) before re-running this assertion.
